name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+19 partisan lean
Incumbent Dan Meuser running for reelection
Prediction markets price Wallace's chances at only about 4%
model.rationale: The R+19 district, an incumbent seeking reelection, and a large fundraising edge all point to a comfortable Meuser win, and markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings signaling otherwise, the fundamentals-based margin of about R+17 stands.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic spending or polling showing Meuser under 55% would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans about nineteen points Republican, making it one of the safer Republican seats on the map. He has raised about $1.9 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Rachel Wallace, who has raised roughly $700,000. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and incumbency. Prediction markets give Wallace only about a 4% chance of an upset. The expected margin is roughly seventeen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling. Any surprise would require an unusually strong Democratic environment or outside intervention in a district that has consistently favored the incumbent's party.
